examples.knowledge_point: Identifying a Complex Number With No Real or No Imaginary Part Represented by an Argand Diagram
examples.problem:
What complex number is represented in the Argand diagram below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035975/assets/7bcf26c8df340bc61e1863043ba2126dea07661c2e288fa5321ddd5ae9e67b46.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the point are $(-4,0).$

- The real part of this complex number is $x=-4,$ and

- the imaginary part is $y=0.$

Therefore, the number depicted is $z=-4+0\textrm{i},$ which can be simplified to $z= -4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035975/assets/6f4759c4401158802661e282a44a0a84e2207ae71d28f38295fe8c6d132d7d46.png)

What complex number is represented in the Argand diagram above?
feedback.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the point are $(-2,-4).$

- The real part of this complex number is $x=-2,$ and

- the imaginary part is $y=-4.$

Therefore, the number depicted is $z=-2-4\text{i}.$ Finally, notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-2-4\text{i} \\  & =-4\text{i}-2.\end{aligned}
$$
